subject: Configurable storage residency + per-tenant TTL — Q&A and roadmap ask
messages:
From: Helen Park <security@acme-corp.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Data residency + retention Qs for Prod rollout

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the demo last week — Acme’s security team has a few follow-ups so we can finalize the production requirements:

1) Can Redwood support per-tenant configurable TTLs (e.g., 30/90/365 days) that are enforced at storage layer and through backups/snapshots?
2) Is it possible to pin an organization’s data to a specific physical region (US-EAST vs EU-WEST)? We need confirmation that data at rest (and snapshot backups) can be kept within that region.
3) How does deletion work for historical KV/cache data and exported artifacts? We need a formal deletion/verification workflow (and evidence we can request).
4) For contracts: can we get a short roadmap + realistic ETA for a pilot and for general availability of these controls?

We can share an internal priority matrix but would like a short technical Q&A and a proposed timeline from product/engineering to share internally.

Appreciate it —
Helen Park
Head of Security, Acme Corporation
--

Subject: Re: Data residency + retention Qs for Prod rollout

Hi all —

We pulled together a short technical Q&A and an initial proposal. Summary below; see attachments for a capabilities matrix and a draft API proposal.

Q1 — Per-tenant TTL enforcement:
- Proposed design: TTL is enforced at the object store layer (metadata + lifecycle policies) and by our garbage-collection pipeline for ephemeral caches/KV. We will add a tenant-scoped TTL configuration API.
- Backups/snapshots: retention policies will be applied to snapshots created after GA; existing snapshots will be considered in migration planning.

Q2 — Regional pinning:
- We can support tenant-level storage region selection for hosted tenants (US-EAST, US-WEST, EU-WEST) by pinning S3 buckets / block volumes to region.
- Guarantee: primary copies and scheduled snapshots will stay in-region. Cross-region replication is disabled unless explicitly requested.

Q3 — Deletion workflow & evidence:
- Deletion runbook: tenant requests → scheduled purge job → post-purge verification job → audit event emitted with verification token.
- Evidence: we will provide an audit record (timestamp, job id, verification hash) and optionally a signed attest document for contracts.

Q4 — Migration path:
- Approach: export → staged reingest into destination region under new storage config → validation → cutover. For large tenants, we propose a pilot migration tool (streaming export) to minimize downtime.

Timeline (proposal):
- Pilot feature (configurable TTL + in-region storage for new tenants): 8–10 weeks after kickoff.
- Migration tooling + snapshot retention enforcement for existing tenants: additional 6–8 weeks.
- GA (full admin UI + audit attestations): 5–6 months, dependent on privacy reviews and legal signoff.

Attachments included: residency-capabilities-matrix.xlsx, retention-api-proposal.md, soc2-data-flow.pdf

Open questions for Acme:
- Priority: do you need support for migration of existing data as part of pilot?
- Which regions are required for pilot (US-EAST only, or EU as well)?

-Karthik
Director, Product Management
Redwood Inference

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Data residency + retention Qs for Prod rollout

Thanks — quick engineering take and constraints: 

- Technical constraints: current multi-tenant storage layer assumes a single default region per deployment; introducing tenant-level bucket pinning requires changes to our provisioning layer and operator workflows.
- Migration approach for 6TB: streaming export + reingest is feasible; estimated reingest SLA ~24–72 hours depending on parallelism and throttles; we need to validate bandwidth with Acme.
- Backups: we can mark snapshots with retention metadata from day one; preventing historic snapshots from leaving the region requires careful snapshot policy changes (we will surface an explicit opt-in).

Proposed high-level milestone plan for Acme (for sharing with legal/procurement):
1) Week 0–2: Kickoff + discovery (confirm data sizes, retention SLAs, legal attestation format).
2) Week 3–6: Pilot build: tenant TTL API + region pinning for new tenants + basic migration script.
3) Week 7–10: Pilot run with Acme tenant (rm validation, daylight testing, signed deletion attestation template).
4) Week 11–18: Migration tooling hardening + GA items (admin UI, automated attestations, audit retention).

Risks/asks: network bandwidth for reingest, a short test window to run a full export.

I can put together a one-page milestone summary and a resource ask (engineer + infra hours) for the kickoff.

—Dylan
Senior Software Engineer, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
